final_candidates.decision_summary: R169K combines strong predicted antibody escape (z=0.810) with maximal sequence plausibility (ESM-1v z=1.000), preserving replication fitness while evading V2-directed antibodies.
Q312R demonstrates the highest immune escape prediction (z=0.876) paired with solid PLM plausibility (z=0.271), balancing potent escape with viable replication competence.
T277A provides high predicted immune escape (z=0.817) at the CD4 binding site region, outperforming alternative candidates despite moderate sequence plausibility.

stop_reason.detail: The top-3 candidates are robustly resolved across escape potential and fitness proxies, rendering additional evidence gathering unnecessary.

history.rationale: R169 is located in the V2 apex supersite (PG9/CAP256 target); R169K provides antibody escape while preserving replication fitness and native trimer assembly.
R169K exhibits both high predicted antibody escape (0.810) and exceptional sequence plausibility (1.000), making it an ideal candidate preserving replication fitness.
R169K exhibits exceptional fitness compatibility across both ESM-1v (1.000) and MSA frequency (0.258), alongside robust EVEscape prediction (0.810).
N330 anchors the N332-glycan supersite; N330D eliminates this glycan to escape PGT121/10-1074 class bNAbs while maintaining high viral replication fitness.
High escape score (0.801) is tempered by very low ESM-1v likelihood (0.002), risking viral replication capacity.
High escape prediction is counterbalanced by complete absence in MSA homologs and negligible PLM plausibility, risking replication fitness.
Disrupts the N330-V-S glycosylation sequon, mediating robust escape from V3-glycan targeting antibodies while retaining basic folding and replication fitness.
Known 2G12/glycan epitope knockout shows moderate escape (0.641) but extremely low ESM-1v viability ratio (0.0007).
Glycan knockout has low evolutionary recurrence and very poor sequence plausibility, indicating replication fitness cost.
Located in loop D of the CD4-binding site; N279K confers strong escape from VRC01-class neutralizing antibodies while remaining well-tolerated for viral replication.
Good escape (0.712) but very low fitness prior (0.001), lowering priority.
Displays lower escape and minimal evolutionary tolerance compared to CD4bs alternatives.
Introduces an acidic charge in loop D of the CD4-binding site, facilitating escape from CD4bs-directed bNAbs while preserving functional envelope conformation.
Strong escape (0.787) but penalized heavily by low sequence plausibility (0.002).
Moderate escape value but low conservation and low MSA representation (1.3%) indicate replication fitness vulnerability.
Abolishes the N275-I-T glycan sequon in loop D, altering CD4bs epitope accessibility for immune escape with minimal fitness defect in DMS.
Strong escape potential (0.817) is partially offset by low PLM support (0.008), though it retains better plausibility than glycan knockouts.
T277A combines high escape potential (0.817) with substantial natural occurrence in homologs (10.4%), securing position 3 despite lower ESM-1v.
Substitutes the V3 crown residue with the conserved consensus Arg, altering sensitivity to V3-directed antibodies while preserving or improving replication fitness.
Q312R achieves the highest escape score (0.876) while maintaining solid PLM plausibility (0.271), balancing escape and replication viability.
Q312R holds the highest EVEscape score (0.876) paired with strong Swiss-Prot homolog tolerance (0.289) and solid PLM plausibility (0.271).
Located in the V3 stem/flank; T317A modulates local conformational dynamics to evade V3-targeting antibodies while retaining replication competence.
Moderate escape (0.616) paired with relatively higher sequence likelihood (0.016) among the remaining pool.
Zero frequency in MSA homologs and low PLM score downgrade its priority despite modest escape score.
D171 is situated near the V2 apex; D171N promotes escape from quaternary V2-directed antibodies while preserving trimer stability.
Lowest escape score in the set (0.584) combined with low sequence likelihood (0.002).
Shows reasonable MSA presence (8.9%) but low escape prediction and weak ESM-1v score.
Resides within the gp41 MPER 2F5 core epitope; S665A impairs 2F5 neutralization without abrogating envelope-mediated viral entry and replication.
Moderate escape (0.611) and weak fitness support (0.005) keep this candidate lower in ranking.
Modest natural frequency (8%) in MPER, but relatively weaker immune escape relative to V2/V3 loop candidates.
